DILG BACONG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION NO. S. 20 FEB 1 1 2025 GLORIA C. AGUHAR City Director — DILG Muntinlupa Field Office Dear Director Aguhar: This has reference to your letter dated 13 June 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion regarding the following matters: I. 2. 3. 4. During the transition period, what specific duties and functions can and cannot be performed by the Successor of Punong Barangay officially? After a permanent vacancy has been determined, is there a specific timeline by which the successor is bound to accept the office and take his/her oath as PB? How do we address the successor appropriately during the transition period, considering under Section 92 (a), he can only assume as Punong Barangay after signifying his/her acceptance of the said office by taking an oath? How do we address the issue wherein the barangay urgently needs to pursue a transaction during the transition period where the presence and/or signature of a Punong Barangay is non-negotiable? (e.g. Bank checks) Per the representation, the Punong Barangay of Buli, Muntinlupa City was tragically shot to death, causing a permanent vacancy in the office of the Punong Barangay. Thus, the request for guidance and legal opinion. As to the first query, please be informed that during transition period and after the successor have taken his oath of office as Punong Barangay and assumed the functions, powers and duties thereof, he/she may already exercise all the official functions of a punong barangay, as provided in Section 3891 of RA 7160, otherwise Section 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. - (a) The punong barangay, as the chief executive of the barangay government, shall exercise such powers and perform such duties and functions, as provided by this Code and other laws. (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, thc punong barangay shall: (1) Enforce all laws and ordinances which are applicable within the barangay; (2) Negotiate, enter into, and sign contracts for and in behalf of the barangay, upon authorization of the sangguniang barangay; (3) Maintain public order in the barangay and, in pursuance thereof, assist the city or municipal mayor and the sanggunian members in the performance of their duties and functions; (4) Call and preside over the sessions of the Sangguniang barangay and the barangay assembly, and vote only to break a tie; (5) Upon approval by a majority of all thc members of the sanggumang barangay, appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials; "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline Nov: 8876-34-54

known as the Local Government Code of 1991, by operation of law under Section 44 (b)2 of the said Code. Nevertheless, during the time the successor has not yet taken his oath of office as the Punong Barangay, he/she cannot perform the duties and functions of a Punong Barangay, and he/she is still considered a member of the Sangguniang Barangay prior to taking his/her oath of office. In line with this, while the successor has not yet formally taken the role of Punong Barangay, they can still participate in preparatory activities, such as orientation sessions or consultations with the outgoing Punong Barangay or his/her staff. However, their participation should be framed as preparatory or advisory, not authoritative. Thus, a successor who has not taken his/her oath of office as Punong Barangay under Section 92 (a)3 of the LGC has no authority yet to perform the functions and duties of a Punong Barangay. Also, said successor who has not taken his/her oath office as Punong Barangay cannot negotiate, enter into, and sign contracts for and in behalf of the barangay, appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials, and approve vouchers relating to the disbursement of barangay funds. As to the second query, Section 44 (b)4 of RA 710, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, is instructive. However, said LGC provision did not provide for the timeline by which the successor is bound to accept the office and take his/her oath as PB. Nonetheless, we are of the considered view that the intent of this provision is to establish a corresponding succession process to ensure that LGUs continue to function efficiently. (b) In the performance of his peace and order functions. the punong barangay shall be entitled to possess and carry the necessary firearm within his territorial jurisdiction, subject to appropriate rules and regulations. 2 DILG opinion NO. 25, s. 2008, 15 April 2008 Section 92. Oath of Office. - (a) All elective and appointive local officials and employees shall, upon assumption to office, subscribe to an oath or affirmation of office in the prescribed form. The oath or affirmation of office shall be filed with the office of the local chief executive concerned. A copy of the oath or affirmation of office of all elective and appointive local officials and employees shall be preserved in the individual personal records file under custody of the personnel office, division, or section of the local government unit concerned. "Section 44. Permanent Vacancies in the Offices of the Govemor, Vice-Govemor, Mayor, and Vice-Mayor. (b) If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the punong barangay, the highest ranking sanggunian barangay member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall become the punong barangay. For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from office, voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office. Thus, the successor should immediately assume the position of Punong Barangay and discharge the duties and functions of a Punong Barangay as mandated by law in order to prevent any disruption in the barangay's functions and to guarantee that governance is uninterrupted. As to the third query, during the transition period and before the successor takes his/her oath of office as Punong Barangay, he/she should be addressed as the "Incoming Punong Barangay" or simply the "Successor" to acknowledge their pending role without implying they have formally assumed the position. Thus, in the official communications or public announcements, state explicitly that the person is the designated successor but has yet to formally assume the office, pending the oath-taking As to the last query, we are of the considered view that in order to address the urgent transactions during the transition period where the presence and/or signature of a Punong Barangay is non-negotiable, the successor should immediately take the oath of office as Punong Barangay to prevent any disruption in the functions of the barangay and to ensure that governance is not disrupted. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY. A ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD,'lasm Copy furnished: MARIA LOURDES L.
